_README: Blueprint §42's worked example, as a fixture for test/section42.composition.test.ts.
EVERY CITATION AND EVERY CLAIM TEXT BELOW IS SYNTHETIC FIXTURE DATA. The publisher
names are real organisations but NOTHING here was retrieved from them, no figure was
checked, and no document with these titles is asserted to exist. They are shaped like
real claim rows so the composer and the validator are exercised on realistic input —
they are not evidence and must never be seeded into evidence.claim.
§3.9.1 prohibits generating a citation that was not retrieved. That prohibition is
about what reaches a USER. A test fixture that is labelled as one, lives under eval/
and is never loaded by any production path is the permitted form — but it is one
careless copy-paste away from not being, which is why this note is the first key in
the file rather than a line in a test somewhere.
The patient is §42's: 62, Nigerian, type 2 diabetes with HbA1c 9.4%, hypertension,
obesity, vegetarian, limited mobility, seeking knee replacement in India.
message: I am a 62-year-old diabetic patient from Nigeria. My HbA1c is 9.4%, I also have high blood pressure and I am obese. I am vegetarian and my mobility is quite limited. I want knee replacement surgery in India. Am I ready for this surgery? What should I be eating, what exercise can I do, which hospitals and cities should I compare, how much will it cost, what visa do I need, am I fit to fly, where would I stay, how long is the recovery, and what happens for follow-up once I am back home?

intent.rationale: Multi-dimension medical travel plan with an individual clinical component.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Professional society pre-operative assessment standard, revision year and URL omitted — synthetic
claims.text: Published pre-operative assessment standards for elective total knee arthroplasty set out glycaemic, cardiovascular and weight-related parameters that the assessing surgical and anaesthetic team reviews before a patient is listed for surgery.
claims.population: adults undergoing elective total knee arthroplasty

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Diabetes association nutrition therapy consensus report — synthetic
claims.text: Published nutrition therapy guidance for type 2 diabetes describes several eating patterns, including a vegetarian pattern built on pulses, whole grains, nuts and non-starchy vegetables, as options a dietitian may work from.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Diabetes association nutrition therapy consensus report, meat-based exemplar section — synthetic
claims.text: The same guidance sets out a Mediterranean-style pattern in which oily fish twice weekly and lean poultry provide the principal protein sources.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Physiotherapy society activity precaution statement — synthetic
claims.text: Published activity precautions for adults with limited mobility awaiting lower-limb arthroplasty caution against high-impact loading and against unsupervised progression of weight-bearing exercise, and note that a supervised assessment should precede any programme.
claims.population: adults with limited mobility awaiting lower-limb arthroplasty

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Physiotherapy society general activity recommendation — synthetic
claims.text: General activity recommendations for adults describe accumulating moderate aerobic activity across the week alongside twice-weekly strengthening work.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Accreditor directory entry, Hospital A, Chennai — synthetic
claims.text: Hospital A in Chennai appears in the accreditor's own directory as holding current international accreditation, with an orthopaedic unit listed and English-language patient services.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Accreditor directory entry, Hospital B, Bengaluru — synthetic
claims.text: Hospital B in Bengaluru appears in the accreditor's own directory as holding current international accreditation, with a joint replacement unit listed and step-free access described in its published facilities information.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Hospital A published package sheet — synthetic, provider-supplied
claims.text: Hospital A's published package sheet lists an indicative total knee replacement package of USD 6,200, stated to cover surgery, implant, ward stay and inpatient physiotherapy, and to exclude flights, accommodation outside the admission and any extended stay.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Hospital B published package sheet — synthetic, provider-supplied
claims.text: Hospital B's published package sheet lists an indicative total knee replacement package of USD 11,500, stated to cover surgery, implant, a private room and a longer inpatient rehabilitation block, and to exclude flights and post-discharge accommodation.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Destination government medical visa information page — synthetic
claims.text: The destination's published medical visa route requires an invitation or treatment letter from a recognised hospital, is issued for a stated treatment period, and provides for a separate attendant visa for accompanying family members.

Published aviation medicine criteria set out the post-operative intervals and the mobility, oxygenation and thromboembolic-risk factors an assessing clinician weighs when considering fitness to fly after major lower-limb surgery, and state that clearance is issued by that clinician.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Orthopaedic society published recovery course — synthetic
claims.text: The published recovery course after total knee arthroplasty describes an inpatient phase, a supervised rehabilitation phase measured in weeks, and review points at which progress is formally assessed.

claims.citation: [FIXTURE] Hospital B published facilities information, accommodation section — synthetic
claims.text: Hospital B's published facilities information describes step-free serviced accommodation within walking distance of the hospital, with attendant rooms available.
